properties.name: Every clippy gate passed locally and BOTH CI jobs failed on the same lint — the flags were identical and the COMPILER was the narrow gate, which is the one axis skill_lint's gate-list cross-check structurally cannot see
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-24 landing increment 4 (PR #329). All six local gates were run and reported green — fmt, clippy on both crates with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`, the core and workspace test suites, eleven python gates and the design gate. Both CI jobs then failed, on one lint:

    error: using `chunks_exact` with a constant chunk size
      --> crates/reflow2-core/src/foundation/store/engine/mod.rs:605:29
      = note: `-D clippy::chunks-exact-to-as-chunks` implied by `-D warnings`

COMMAND IDENTICAL, FLAGS IDENTICAL. Local was rustc/clippy **1.94.0**; CI runs `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`, which is **1.98.0**, and 1.98 added `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`. The lint did not exist on the developer machine, so no local invocation of any width could have produced it.

⭐ WHY THIS IS NOT BL-159 AGAIN, THOUGH IT LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE IT. BL-159 was the same SYMPTOM — documented gate followed exactly, build still red — and its cause was a FLAGS difference (`-p reflow2-core` clippy lacking `-D warnings`). `skill_lint.py` now cross-checks AGENTS.md's gate block against `ci.yml` for coverage, identity and fidelity, and it closed that hole properly. **It cannot close this one.** Both records it compares are TEXT IN THIS REPOSITORY, and the toolchain version is in NEITHER: `@stable` names a moving target, so AGENTS.md can name the exact command with the exact flags, skill_lint can confirm all four checks, and the gate is still narrower locally than in CI. The cross-check is complete over what is written down and blind to what resolves at run time.

FIXED AT THE CAUSE rather than by chasing the symptom: `rustup update stable` (1.94.0 → 1.98.0), then the whole sweep re-run, which found exactly ONE more finding and no others. Fixing the reported line alone would have left the machine two minor versions behind and the next lint would have arrived the same way.

⚠️ THE FINDING WAS THEN ALLOWED, NOT FIXED. clippy is right that `as_chunks::<4>()` is better, and `dec:absorb-the-foundation-subset-and-end-the-dependency` requires the absorbed files to stay byte-diffable against dynograph-foundation v0.12.0 — the same ground as `graphalg`'s `#![allow(dead_code)]`, where Anthony said "don't trim now - if we decide it isn't necessary, then we can trim in the future." The allow carries that reasoning at the call site. **Absorbed code makes every future lint bump a provenance decision, not a cleanup**, and that cost was not named when the absorption was scoped.

⭐⭐ THE SHAPE THIS BELONGS TO. This is the FIFTH instance in two days of a narrow gate read as a wide one: `#[cfg(test)]` invisible to the test run; feature-gated files invisible to `--no-default-features` clippy; doctests invisible to build and clippy; a non-snake-case test name invisible without `--all-targets`; and now a lint invisible to an older compiler. The first four are a local HABIT and can be fixed by remembering. **This one cannot** — no amount of care with flags reaches it, because the gate's width is set by a binary nobody versioned in the record. Recorded here rather than as advice: the only defence that worked was CI running the wide form, and the only durable fix is keeping the local toolchain pinned to what CI resolves.

📌 OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, worth knowing before the next session: the toolchain update means the next cargo command pays a full rebuild including the ~19-minute librocksdb-sys C++ compile.
